sections.h2: Picking up your car at Malaga Airport
sections.html: Malaga is one of Europe’s busiest car hire airports. Some companies have desks in the arrivals area with cars in the airport car parks; many others, including several low-cost local suppliers, are off-airport and take you to their depot by shuttle bus. Your voucher shows where to meet. Off-airport can mean queues at busy times, so allow extra time.

Fuel policy is the biggest thing to check at Malaga. A full to full policy (collect it full, return it full) is usually the fairest. With “full to empty” you pay up front for a tank of fuel, often with a service charge, and get no refund for fuel you don’t use. Also check the excess and the deposit, as some local suppliers hold a large deposit unless you buy their own cover.

sections.h2: Driving on the Costa del Sol
sections.html: Spain drives on the right. The coast road links Malaga with Marbella, Fuengirola and Nerja, and inland routes lead to Ronda, Granada, Córdoba and Seville. The AP-7 toll motorway runs parallel to the free coastal road for part of the way.

faqs.q: Is cheap car hire at Malaga worth it?
faqs.a: It can be, but compare the total cost. A low headline price can come with a full-to-empty fuel policy, a large deposit or expensive insurance at the desk. Compare like for like before you book.
